name: media_rss_sweep
what: Live RSS sweep of 8 popular Indian newspapers' section feeds -- Economic Times, Hindu, Hindu Business Line, Times of India, Livemint, Moneycontrol, Business Standard (English) + Amar Ujala (Hindi) -- filtered for investment-intent language (English + Devanagari keywords), matched against real 23-country foreign stock-market rosters (same files layer 42 uses). Full article text pulled only for roster-confirmed hits. Originally a workaround for ET/Hindu/HBL blocking Anthropic's hosted crawler/search infra outright -- runs via subprocess curl from the local machine, which is never blocked (see feedback_economic_times_blocked memory) -- kept as the standard fetch method when extended to more sources for consistency. CAVEAT on the Hindi source: company-name matching only catches names Indian financial press conventionally leaves in Latin script (Apple, Tesla, Toyota); transliterated names (e.g. एप्पल for Apple) are invisible to the shared Latin-script matcher -- partial, not full, non-English coverage. Separate CAVEAT: 'strong' fragment matches on generic industry-descriptive company names (e.g. 'Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp' vs. any article about semiconductor manufacturing in general) still slip through even after the SPAC/share-class filter -- treat every match here as a candidate for human review via its full_text field, not a confirmed lead, same as layer 44's un-reviewed MoU rows.

The company filings say several Indian states began seizing the stock straight away.MORE CHALLENGES, RELIEF FOR SOME FIRMSThe energy drink market in India boomed after PepsiCo launched Sting in 2017, with its 20-rupee ($0.21) plastic bottles proving popular among 15- to 19-year-olds and in rural areas, Euromonitor says. matches.title: Haier, Godrej, Blue Star failed to detect fake e-waste recycling claims, India notice shows
matches.full_text: Indian tax authorities have faulted appliance makers Haier, Godrej & Boyce and Blue Star for not detecting documents fabricated by a spurious recycler who did no e-waste work, while relying on them to meet green goals, a government notice showed.The third-biggest generator of e-waste after China and the United States, India has been concerned that 78% of the waste from discarded electronic goods is processed by informal scrap dealers who use methods that harm the environment.Reuters reviewed an August 27 notice sent to the three home appliance majors that detailed the lapses. Indian officials also accused them of wrongly claiming tax credits of $714,000 for recycling services that were never actually rendered. The foundational activity of procurement, receipt and processing of e-waste itself is not established,  the tax officials said in their 550-page notice.Godrej & Boyce and Blue Star said they would respond to the notice and were committed to legal compliance, adding that the recycler concerned had been authorised by the government.Godrej said it followed all government guidelines for recycling, while Blue Star said it had no reason to believe any irregularity but had stopped dealings with the vendor.Haier India said it would continue to cooperate with the authorities and was committed to legal compliance.India's finance ministry did not respond to queries.ALARM AMONG CONSUMER ELECTRONICS COMPANIESThe findings have set off alarm in India's $95-billion consumer electronics market as many big companies aware of the case have launched internal reviews of recycling supply chains, three industry executives said on condition of anonymity.Haier and Godrej sell appliances such as refrigerators and washing machines in India, while Mumbai-listed Blue Star specialises in air-conditioning. They compete with market leaders such as Samsung and LG.India allows companies to claim credits for tax paid on services such as recycling, reducing the amount of tax owed on their sales. Penalties for false claims can run up to 100%.The incident follows a January warning by the government against  fraudulent certification  issued by spurious recyclers.Since 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government has asked companies to recycle a share of the products they sell each year, but most meet those obligations by buying compliance certificates from recyclers who do the actual work.NO VERIFICATION, TAX CREDITSThe notice cited a little-known Indian recycler, WEEE-PRO Resource Recovery Solutions, as the issuer of the compliance certificates.It accused the three companies of not having verified the vendor was doing actual work, but relying instead on fabricated documents to prove compliance.WEEE-PRO did not respond to Reuters queries. matches.title: Midwest Energy to set up Rs 250-crore rare earth magnet plant in Hyderabad
matches.full_text: Hyderabad-based Midwest Energy is setting up Indiaâs first sintered NdFeB magnet plant in Hyderabad at an initial investment of Rs 250 crore to build domestic capacity for a product India currently imports almost entirely. The plant is undergoing trial production with commercial production expected to begin by mid-October with an initial 500 MT/year capacity, sources said.The plant will manufacture magnets -- using manufacturing tech developed in-house -- for electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, smartphones, defence applications and MRI equipment, with sample testing underway with several EV and wind-energy companies.India currently imports almost 100% of its sintered rare earth permanent magnet requirements. Midwest Energyâs plant could eventually help replace around 15-20% of Indiaâs import dependence over the next three to five years, sources added.At the initial 500-tonne scale, the companyâs magnets are expected to be around 20-25% more expensive than Chinese imports. The company is also in the process of expanding its capacity to 5,000 tonnes by December 2027 at an investment of up to Rs 2,000 crore to help bring costs closer to Chinese levels.Alongside the rare-earth magnet business, the technology and clean energy arm of Midwest Business House also has a 1.2 GW battery energy storage system plant in Bengaluru that began commercial production in July this year.

matches.title: Reliance Retail, 7-Eleven end a five-year India franchise deal as convenience stores struggle
matches.full_text: Mumbai: Reliance Retail and 7-Eleven are ending their five-year franchisee deal in India, closing most of the nearly 60 convenience stores they operated under the partnership, after struggling to make the format profitable, people familiar with the matter said.A handful of outlets are clearing the inventory before shutting, they said. 7-Eleven may look for another Indian partner to keep a foothold in the market, although no decision has been made, the people said.The exit highlights an unusual squeeze that convenience stores are facing in India, with millions of small kirana stores that have long served consumers' immediate needs on one side and quick-commerce companies that are bringing the same snacks, groceries and daily essentials to doorsteps within minutes on the other.134679627Reliance and 7-Eleven did not respond to ET's queries.The partnership, struck in 2021, was intended to bring the world's largest convenience-store chain to India through Reliance's retail network. But the business struggled to achieve the scale needed to offset the relatively high costs of running branded stores.The 7-India Convenience Retail venture reported revenue of about â¹92 crore ($10.6 million) and a net loss of nearly â¹90 crore in the year ended March 2026, according to its financial statements. Reliance wants to reach consumers across every channel, but sustainability ultimately matters. Convenience stores have faced increasing pressure from quick commerce since the pandemic, with both formats offering similar assortments and serving the same immediate-needs occasions,  said Devangshu Dutta, founder and CEO of Third Eyesight, a consumer-sector consultancy. Kiranas operate with far lower overheads and different margin expectations than corporate-run convenience stores. Reliance's exit could therefore signal a broader rethink of the format, particularly in markets where quick commerce has become a strong alternative. Globally convenience stores have become powerful retail businesses in several markets despite the expansion of supermarkets and hypermarkets. 7-Eleven in Japan, Taiwan, Thailand and Singapore; Lawson in Japan and Oxxo in Mexico are among the largest retailers in their respective markets.7-Eleven's Japanese parent, Seven & i Holdings, operates more than 85,000 stores globally, making it one of the world's largest retail networks. Yet the company has been restructuring its overseas operations and closing stores in North America as consumer behaviour and store economics change.In India, however, organised convenience retail has struggled to replicate the success seen in other Asian and emerging markets. matches.title: GAIL’s Sanjay Kumar named next Petronet LNG CEO
matches.full_text: Sanjay Kumar, Director (Marketing) at state-owned GAIL (India) Ltd, has been named the next Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Petronet LNG Ltd. His term will begin on May 13, 2027, following the conclusion of current CEO A K Singh's extended tenure.Petronet's board finalized the decision during a 15-minute meeting on October 2, as disclosed in a regulatory filing. Kumar, 59, has been appointed for a five-year tenure.Also read: India's crude imports hit 2026 high in September as Gulf supplies surge despite Hormuz risksAs India's largest liquefied natural gas importer, Petronet is majority-owned by state-run energy companies, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), GAIL (India) Ltd, Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC), and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) each holding a 12.5% stake. Although chaired by the Union Petroleum Secretary, Petronet is registered as a private limited entity. Consequently, it operates outside the jurisdiction of government watchdogs such as the CAG, CVC, and RTI. Board executives are subject to a retirement age of 65, compared to 60 at public sector units, and receive higher compensation than PSU counterparts.Kumar, who has served as GAIL's Marketing Director since mid-June 2023, holds a mechanical engineering degree from IIT Kharagpur and an MBA. He brings more than 35 years of industry experience across the natural gas and LNG value chain.Petronet LNG manages India's premier LNG import facility at Dahej in Gujarat alongside a second terminal at Kochi in Kerala. Together, these facilities offer a combined regasification capacity of 27.5 million tonnes per annum (MMTPA) - 22.5 MMTPA at Dahej and 5 MMTPA at Kochi. The company manages roughly 74% of the nation's LNG imports and fulfills about 34% of overall gas consumption.Also read: G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, a boost for TrumpThis leadership change coincides with national efforts to boost natural gas within the energy mix and expand gas infrastructure. To support these goals, Petronet is advancing plans to increase Dahej's regasification capacity, build a greenfield LNG facility on the east coast, and construct a petrochemical project at Dahej.

matches.title: Canon eyes chip projects, plans local service centres in India
matches.full_text: Japanese imaging and optical major Canon had discussions with all those engaged in key semiconductor manufacturing projects in India and plans to bring its technology and service centres to the country, said its India President and CEO Toshiaki Nomura. Canon, a global supplier of lithography systems used in semiconductor manufacturing, said it is looking to support the development of India's semiconductor ecosystem as the government steps up efforts to establish domestic chip fabrication capabilities. The Japanese technology major is sensing a "great opportunity" in the upcoming semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem promoted by the government, and the company will bring its technologies (lithographic machines) to help assist chip manufacturers to produce chips in India, he said. "Now everybody knows semiconductor manufacturing is the buzzword in India. We have a lithographic machine to produce those chips... We bring our technologies to help assist the chip manufacturer to produce chips in India. So that's a great opportunity for us," Nomura told PTI. He said Canon has already engaged with major semiconductor projects that are currently under development in the country. Asked whether the company has held discussions with semiconductor ventures being established in India, he said, "Yes, we have discussed with all those key manufacturers. The projects are ongoing and, as and when some development is confirmed, we will share it."

matches.title: Credit offtake stays ahead of banks' deposit growth
matches.full_text: MUMBAI: Advance growth continued to outstrip deposit growth at several banks in the second quarter of FY27, with loan books expanding at a double-digit pace across public sector and mid-sized private lenders despite efforts to accelerate deposit mobilisation.Provisional business updates for Q2FY27 show advances growing between 13% and 29% year-on-year across the banks, with smaller and regional lenders generally recording faster expansion than their larger peers. Tamilnad Mercantile Bank led the pack with 29.4% growth in advances, followed by Karnataka Bank at 24.9%, UCO Bank at 24.8% and J&K Bank at 23.7%.Among larger public sector banks, Bank of India reported the fastest credit growth at 20.4%, followed by Canara Bank at 19.3%, Punjab & Sind Bank at 19.4%, Union Bank of India at 18.5% and Bank of Baroda at 18.3%. Punjab National Bank's advances grew 14.8%, while Indian Bank reported 16.6% growth.Deposit growth, however, was more uneven. Bank of India's deposits rose 21.6%, ahead of its 20.4% credit growth, while Bank of Baroda's deposits grew 16.7%, broadly keeping pace with its 18.3% advance growth. Canara Bank's deposits rose 13.1% against 19.3% credit growth, while Union Bank's deposits grew 6.9% against 18.5% loan growth. At PNB, deposits grew 9.9%, compared with 14.8% growth in advances.The divergence was more pronounced among some mid-sized lenders. UCO Bank's advances grew 24.8%, compared with 14.2% deposit growth, while J&K Bank reported 23.7% credit growth against 16.3% deposit growth. Karnataka Bank's advances rose 24.9%, more than twice the 12% growth in deposits.Some lenders, however, managed to expand deposits faster than advances. Tamilnad Mercantile Bank's deposits grew 25.5%, compared with 29.4% growth in advances, while Dhanlaxmi Bank reported deposit growth of 20.2% against 22.3% credit growth. At South Indian Bank, both advances and deposits grew 18.7%.The numbers point to continued pressure on banks to mobilise deposits even as credit demand remains firm.You use AI every day. Lockheed Martin is considering a further expansion of its manufacturing footprint in India if it secures the contract to supply medium transport aircraft to the Indian armed forces, a senior company executive said, according to PTI.India floated a tender in August to acquire 60 medium transport aircraft under a deal estimated at $10.5 billion.Five Indian firms â Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL), Mahindra Group, Adani Defence & Aerospace, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Reliance Defence, are competing for the project. The selected Indian partner is expected to collaborate with a global aircraft manufacturer as part of the programme."We have a long partnership with Tata that produces components and empennages of the C-130J aircraft. It is a very robust capability that will be expanded in our current bid," said Dan Tenney, Senior Vice President, global business development and strategy, Lockheed Martin, according to PTI."We are looking to expand that capability with production and other things that occur within India," he said.Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) has teamed up with Lockheed Martin for the bid, while Mahindra Group has partnered with Brazilian aerospace firm Embraer."So we're very excited by that. India has been a great partner in helping to enable advanced capabilities for that aircraft and beyond," Tenney stated.Tenney said a successful bid by Lockheed Martin and TASL would lead to an expansion of the companyâs existing network in India."So we are looking to do that," Tenney added.Under Lockheed Martinâs proposal, 12 aircraft would be supplied in flyaway condition, while the remaining 48 would be built in India.Lockheed Martin has additionally offered to modernise the Indian Air Forceâs (IAF) 12 existing C-130J aircraft to the proposed upgraded configuration. If implemented, the move could create a standardised fleet of 72 aircraft for the IAF.The C-130J fleet has logged more than 58,000 flight hours and has been deployed for a range of missions, including operations at high altitudes in Ladakh, humanitarian assistance during floods in Nepal and the evacuation of Indian citizens from Sudan in 2023.
Taiwan receives first US-made F-16Vs
Meanwhile, Taiwan on Friday took delivery of its first US-built F-16V fighter jets as the island moves to strengthen its defence capabilities amid the threat of a potential military assault by China, as per AFP.
The two aircraft are part of an $8 billion agreement for 66 F-16Vs, approved during US President Donald Trump's first term, with deliveries scheduled to take place this year.
The delivery comes as Taiwan waits for Washington to approve a separate $14 billion arms package. Trump has put that deal on hold following objections from China.
Beijing considers Taiwan part of its territory and has not ruled out using force to bring the island under its control.

Ross Benes, senior analyst at eMarketer, described the choice as an attempt to reinforce Ellison's position within the newly combined business.âThe name is ego-driven. It reminds everyone that the most iconic Hollywood brands answer to Ellison and it is his company who won out,â Benes said.Skydance Corporation to debut on NYSEThe company's legal name is scheduled to change to Skydance Corporation on October 6, according to a regulatory filing.On the same day, its Class B shares are expected to move from Nasdaq to the New York Stock Exchange. It is now looking to strengthen its micro-distribution network to reach Tier II and Tier III towns."We are building a strong distribution network through a hub and spoke model, building a closed-loop supply chain across battery deployment, buyback, refurbishment and second-life applications. We are currently working in the e-rickshaw segment, which itself is a large market estimated at around 50 lakh vehicles. We will ramp up our presence in this segment," Biswas told PTI."We also see a huge opportunity in the L5 E-auto, BESS and second-life products. We already have an existing distribution network, and we are looking to expand our network in the existing markets. This will enable us to tap into this growing demand efficiently," he added.Highlighting the market potential in the e-auto and four-wheeler segment, Biswas noted that starting next year, close to 8,000 to 10,000 electric autos are expected to come up for battery replacement, generating substantial demand for new lithium-ion batteries.The batteries retrieved during replacement will also serve as a key raw material source for second-life applications and new battery minerals. matches.full_text: Japanese imaging and optical major Canon had discussions with all those engaged in key semiconductor manufacturing projects in India and plans to bring its technology and service centres to the country, said its India President and CEO Toshiaki Nomura.Canon, a global supplier of lithography systems used in semiconductor manufacturing, said it is looking to support the development of India's semiconductor ecosystem as the government steps up efforts to establish domestic chip fabrication capabilities.The Japanese technology major is sensing a "great opportunity" in the upcoming semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem promoted by the government, and the company will bring its technologies (lithographic machines) to help assist chip manufacturers to produce chips in India, he said."Now everybody knows semiconductor manufacturing is the buzzword in India. We have a lithographic machine to produce those chips... We bring our technologies to help assist the chip manufacturer to produce chips in India. So that's a great opportunity for us," Nomura told PTI.He said Canon has already engaged with major semiconductor projects that are currently under development in the country.Asked whether the company has held discussions with semiconductor ventures being established in India, he said, "Yes, we have discussed with all those key manufacturers. The projects are ongoing and, as and when some development is confirmed, we will share it." India has been actively promoting semiconductor manufacturing through incentive schemes and has approved multiple projects across semiconductor fabrication, assembly, testing, marking and packaging segments as part of its broader strategy to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem.Nomura said the progress of semiconductor projects in India could also pave the way for Canon to establish dedicated support infrastructure for chip manufacturing customers in the country."Once the project is confirmed, of course we need 24x7 support to the chip manufacturer. In that sense, we will bring our technologies and service centres in India. That's our plan," he said.On whether India's ambitious timelines for developing a semiconductor ecosystem are achievable, Nomura expressed confidence in the country's capabilities."I believe in the power of India. We cannot control the timeline itself, as it is the chip manufacturer's responsibility. But this will come in the near future. That's our expectation," he said.The executive also acknowledged the efforts being made by policymakers and industry stakeholders to develop the ecosystem required for semiconductor manufacturing."Governments and related parties are working very hard to build up this ecosystem. matches.title: Sebi keeps Inox Clean Energy's IPO papers to raise ₹10K cr in abeyance
matches.full_text: Markets regulator Sebi has kept in 'abeyance' the draft offer documents of Inox Clean Energy Ltd, which is looking to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 8,000 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares, amounting to Rs 2,000 crore by promoter Devansh Jain, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).The status of the issue was updated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday under the list of IPOs whose observations have been kept in abeyance.The company had filed its draft papers with the regulator on September 29.Without specifying reasons, the regulator stated that the "issuance of observations (has been) kept in abeyance", according to an update on its website.The proposed issue could rank among the largest IPOs in India's private-sector renewable energy space.Inox Clean Energy, part of the INOXGFL Group, proposes to use the proceeds from the fresh issue primarily for repayment or prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings of the company and its subsidiaries, besides general corporate purposes.The company operates an integrated renewable energy platform with two principal businesses renewable power generation and solar manufacturing.As of August 31, 2026, its renewable independent power producer (IPP) portfolio stood at 9.29 GW across India and Africa. This included 2.37 GW of operational capacity, with around 0.80 GW under construction, 2.99 GW of pipeline capacity and 3.13 GW of future capacity, according to the DRHP.Its solar manufacturing business has an operational solar module manufacturing capacity of 6 GW across India and the US, while solar cell manufacturing capacity is under construction in India and the US.After the IPO, Inox Clean Energy will compete with a growing number of listed renewable energy companies, including Adani Green Energy, NTPC Green Energy, ACME Solar Holdings, Waaree Energies, Premier Energies, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions and JSW Energy.The company is part of the broader INOXGFL Group, which has interests in chemicals and renewable energy. The group has three listed entities - Gujarat Fluorochemicals Ltd, Inox Wind Ltd and Inox Green Energy Services Ltd.The group has integrated capabilities spanning solar module manufacturing, wind power generation, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) and renewable energy operations and maintenance.Nuvama Wealth Management, CLSA India, Emirates NBD Capital India, HSBC Securities and Capital Markets (India), ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services, JM Financial, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors and UBS Securities India are the book-running lead managers to the issue.
